The '''58th Academy Awards''' ceremony, organized by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), took place on March 24, 1986, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in [[Los Angeles]] beginning at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 9:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 23 categories honoring [[1985 in film|films released in 1985]]. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Stanley Donen]] and directed by [[Marty Pasetta]].<ref name="NYT">{{cite news|title=58th Annual Academy Awards Presentation |url=https://www.nytimes.com/tv/show/38875/58th-Annual-Academy-Awards-Presentation/details |access-date=Jun 9, 2015 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url-access=limited |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626152029/http://www.nytimes.com/tv/show/38875/58th-Annual-Academy-Awards-Presentation/details |archive-date=June 26, 2015}}</ref> Actors [[Alan Alda]], [[Jane Fonda]], and [[Robin Williams]] co-hosted the show. Fonda hosted the gala for the second time, having previously been a co-host of the [[49th Academy Awards|49th ceremony]] held in 1977. Meanwhile, this was Alda and Williams's first Oscars hosting stint.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hosting Chores |url=https://variety.com/2005/film/awards/hosting-chores-1117917933/ |access-date=17 April 2014 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=February 13, 2005 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419022509/http://variety.com/2005/film/awards/hosting-chores-1117917933/ |archive-date=19 April 2014 }}</ref> Eight days earlier, in a ceremony held at [[The Beverly Hilton]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]], on March 16, the [[Academy Award for Technical Achievement|Academy Awards for Technical Achievement]] were presented by host [[Macdonald Carey]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Past Scientific & Technical Awards Ceremonies|url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|access-date=July 31, 2013|publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213185729/http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|archive-date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

''[[Out of Africa (film)|Out of Africa]]'' won seven awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]]. Meanwhile, fellow Best Picture nominee ''[[The Color Purple (1985 film)|The Color Purple]]'' failed to win any of its eleven nominations.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Harmetz |first1=Aljean |title=Oscars Go to ''Out of Africa'' and Its Director, Sydney Pollack |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/03/25/movies/oscars-go-to-out-of-africa-and-its-director-sydney-pollack.html |access-date=June 9, 2015 |work=The New York Times |url-access=limited |date=March 25, 1986 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150524193106/http://www.nytimes.com/1986/03/25/movies/oscars-go-to-out-of-africa-and-its-director-sydney-pollack.html |archive-date=May 24, 2015 }}</ref><ref name="Baltake">{{cite news|last1=Baltake |first1=Joe |title=7 Oscars Come ''Out of Africa'' |url=http://articles.philly.com/1986-03-25/entertainment/26085248_1_oscars-prizzi-s-honor-karen-blixen |access-date=June 9, 2015 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=March 25, 1986 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150624172324/http://articles.philly.com/1986-03-25/entertainment/26085248_1_oscars-prizzi-s-honor-karen-blixen |archive-date=June 24, 2015}}</ref> Other winners included ''[[Cocoon (film)|Cocoon]]'' and ''[[Witness (1985 film)|Witness]]'' with two awards and ''[[Anna & Bella]]'', ''[[Back to the Future]]'', ''[[Broken Rainbow (film)|Broken Rainbow]]'', ''[[Kiss of the Spider Woman (1985 film)|Kiss of the Spider Woman]]'', ''[[Mask (1985 film)|Mask]]'', ''[[Molly's Pilgrim]]'', ''[[The Official Story]]'', ''[[Prizzi's Honor]]'', ''[[Ran (film)|Ran]]'', ''[[The Trip to Bountiful]]'', ''[[White Nights (1985 film)|White Nights]]'', and ''[[Witness to War: Dr. Charlie Clements]]'' with one. The telecast received mixed reviews, and it garnered 37.8&nbsp;million viewers in the United States.

==Winners and nominees==
<!-- Please do not add any fact or statement below unless you have a credible source verifying it. Otherwise, it will be promptly removed. -->
The nominees for the 58th Academy Awards were announced on February 4, 1986, by Academy president [[Robert Wise]] and actress [[Patty Duke]].<ref>{{cite news |title=No Clear Favorite in Oscar Race |work=[[Vancouver Sun]] |date=February 5, 1986 |page=D13}}</ref> ''[[The Color Purple (1985 film)|The Color Purple]]'' and ''[[Out of Africa (film)|Out of Africa]]'' led all nominees with eleven each.<ref>{{cite news|last=Matthews |first=Jack |title=''Out of Africa'' Ties 'Color Purple' as Oscar Nominees : 11 Citations; Spielberg Not Named |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1986-02-05-mn-4345-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |url-access=subscription |date=February 5, 1986 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103081217/http://articles.latimes.com/1986-02-05/news/mn-4345_1_color-purple |archive-date=November 3, 2012 }}</ref> Winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 24, 1986.<ref name="Baltake"/> With its 11 nominations and zero wins, ''The Color Purple'' joined 1977's ''[[The Turning Point (1977 film)|The Turning Point]]'' as the most nominated films in Oscar history without a single win.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Friendly |first1=David T. |title=Academy Hits Racism Accusation |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1986-03-27-ca-1097-story.html |access-date=June 9, 2015 |work=Los Angeles Times |url-access=subscription |date=March 27, 1986 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611054717/http://articles.latimes.com/1986-03-27/entertainment/ca-1097_1_color-purple |archive-date=June 11, 2015 }}</ref> By virtue of her father [[John Huston|John]] and grandfather [[Walter Huston|Walter]]'s wins for Best Director and Best Supporting Actor respectively for 1948's ''[[The Treasure of the Sierra Madre (film)|The Treasure of the Sierra Madre]]'', Best Supporting Actress winner [[Anjelica Huston]] made them the first three-generation Oscar winning family.<ref>{{cite news|last1=King |first1=Susan |title=Calendar Goes to the Oscars: Side Orders |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-03-28-ca-16083-story.html |access-date=June 9, 2015 |work=Los Angeles Times |url-access=subscription |issue=March 28, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611021724/http://articles.latimes.com/1993-03-28/entertainment/ca-16083_1_actor-oscar |archive-date=June 11, 2015 }}</ref> For the first time in Oscars history, all lead acting nominees were born in the United States.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=1151}}</ref> Argentina's ''[[The Official Story]]'' became the first [[Latin America]]n film to win the [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] category.<ref name="TBN">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=676}}</ref>

==Ceremony information==
Determined to revive interest surrounding the awards and reverse declining ratings, the Academy hired [[Stanley Donen]] in December 1985 to produce the telecast for the first time.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Ryan|first1=Desmond|title=Why are old films tinted? Just blame it on the kids.|page=I2|date=December 15, 1985|work=The Philadelphia Inquirer}}</ref> The following February, actor and comedian [[Robin Williams]] was selected as host of the 1986 telecast.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Blakey|first1=Scott|page=45|title=KQEC's ''3-2-1 Contact'' Tries 3-2-1 Blast-Off|date=February 11, 1986|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]}}</ref> Actor [[Alan Alda]] and two-time Oscar-winning actress [[Jane Fonda]] were later announced to join Williams in sharing emceeing duties.<ref>{{cite news|page=D13|title=Alda, Fonda named hosts of Oscars|date=February 28, 1986|work=[[Montreal Gazette]]}}</ref>

Several other people were involved with the production of the ceremony. [[Marty Pasetta]] was hired as director of the telecast.<ref name="NYT"/> [[Lionel Newman]] served as musical director and conductor for the ceremony.<ref>{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=413}}</ref> Actress [[Teri Garr]] performed the titular song from ''[[Flying Down to Rio]]'' during the opening segment.<ref name="Rio">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=673}}</ref> Singer [[Irene Cara]] sang the [[Frank Sinatra]] song "Here's to the Losers" in honor of unsuccessful Oscar nominees throughout history.<ref name="Rio" /> A song-and-dance number featuring actor and singer [[Howard Keel]] and several actresses including [[Cyd Charisse]], [[Leslie Caron]], and [[Debbie Reynolds]] paid tribute to [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]] musicals.<ref name="TBN"/>

===Box office performance of nominated films===
At the time of the nominations announcement on February 5, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $119 million with an average of $23.9 million.<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars>{{cite web|title=1985 Academy Award Nominations and Winner for Best Picture |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1985&p=.htm |access-date=June 17, 2014 |publisher=[[Box Office Mojo]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140614052155/http://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1985&p=.htm |archive-date=June 14, 2014 }}</ref> ''Witness'' was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees with $68.7&nbsp;million in the domestic box office receipts. The film was followed by ''Out of Africa'' ($55.6&nbsp;million), ''The Color Purple'' ($46.4&nbsp;million), ''Prizzi's Honor'' ($26.7&nbsp;million) and ''Kiss of the Spider Woman'' ($13.4&nbsp;million).<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars />

Of the 50 grossing films of the year, 42 nominations went to 12 films on the list. Only ''Back to the Future'' (1st), ''Cocoon'' (4th), ''Witness'' (5th), ''Jagged Edge'' (20th), ''The Color Purple'' (21st), ''Prizzi's Honor'' (30th), ''Agnes of God'' (32nd) were nominated for Best Picture, directing, acting, or screenplay.<ref name="boxofficemojooscars">{{cite web|title=1985 Domestic Grosses (as of February 4, 1987) |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1986-02-04&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1985&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |access-date=May 25, 2014 |publisher=Box Office Mojo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924162923/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1986-02-04&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1985&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |archive-date=September 24, 2015 }}</ref> The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were ''Rambo: First Blood Part II'' (2nd), ''Mask'' (14th), ''White Nights'' (22nd), ''Silverado'' (27th), ''Young Sherlock Holmes'' (44th), and ''Ladyhawke'' (46th).<ref name="boxofficemojooscars" />

===Critical reviews===
Terrence O'Flaherty of the ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'' wrote, "Last night's sustained-release Oscar pill moved faster through the system than most, but from a standpoint of taste it was the worst in years." Regarding Alda, Fonda, and Williams's hosting performance, he commented, "Together they immediately placed a fatal suggestion in the viewer's mind that there must be a shortage of elegant people in the movie business today."<ref>{{cite news|last1=O'Flaherty|first1=Terrence|title=A Very Tacky Night in Hollywood|work=San Francisco Chronicle |date=March 25, 1986|page=55}}</ref> ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' film critic [[Gene Siskel]] noted that after co-host Williams opened the ceremony with a slew of humorous jokes, "The show regrettably returned to its old bad habits with a boring onstage production number intended to be a tribute to old movies."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Siskel |first1=Gene |title='Africa' Dominates With 7 Oscars While ''Purple'' Is Shut Out |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-03-25-8601220307-story.html|access-date=April 4, 2022 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |url-status=live |date=March 25, 1986  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304093144/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1986-03-25/news/8601220307_1_john-huston-anjelica-huston-color-purple |archive-date=March 4, 2016 }}</ref> ''[[The Record (Bergen County)|The Record]]'''s Joel Pisetzner remarked, "The program might as well have begun with the announcement 'Dead, from L.A. it's Academy night!' "<ref>{{cite news|last1=Pisetzner|first1=Joel|title=Again the Stars Come Out for a Glorious Night of Blah|work=[[The Record (Bergen County)|The Record]]|date=March 25, 1986|page=B1}}</ref>

Television columnist [[John J. O'Connor (journalist)|John J. O'Connor]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' quipped, "Suddenly, it seemed, somebody had listened to the complaints that had grown deadeningly familiar over the years." He also added, "Mr. Williams's improvisational, on-the-precipice style of humor brought the event's comic tone thumpingly into the 1980s."<ref>{{cite news|last1=O'Connor |first1=John J. |title=The Academy Awards Ceremony |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/03/26/movies/the-academy-awards-ceremony.html |access-date=August 24, 2015 |work=The New York Times |url-access=limited |date=March 25, 1986 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812213954/http://www.nytimes.com/1986/03/26/movies/the-academy-awards-ceremony.html |archive-date=August 12, 2014 }}</ref> Yardena Arar from the ''[[Los Angeles Daily News]]'' said, "This time, the ABC telecast didn't drown in the thank yous–or, for that matter, boring presentation speeches and production numbers." Furthermore, she observed, "The writing was by and large brisk, the production numbers fair (in the case of the Oscar-nominated songs) to fabulous (Keel's medley with a bevy of former leading ladies)."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Arar|first1=Yardena|title=The Real Winner Was the Audience|work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |date=March 25, 1986|page=8}}</ref> ''[[Houston Chronicle]]'' television critic Ann Hodges remarked, "Oscar 1986 goes into the record books as a very good year–the year the Academy parked the pompous and let the show biz show." She also lauded the winners' acceptance speeches and the various musical numbers during the broadcast.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hodges|first1=Ann|title=Hollywood Blowout Goes Down a Winner|work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=March 25, 1986|page=5}}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 37.8 million people over its length, which was a 2% decrease from the [[57th Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Morales |first1=Tatiana |date=March 24, 2003 |title=TV Ratings for Oscars Plunge |agency=[[CBS News]] |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tv-ratings-for-oscars-plunge/ |url-status=live |access-date=March 12, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220305082006/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tv-ratings-for-oscars-plunge/ |archive-date=March 5, 2022}}</ref> Moreover, the show drew lower [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony with 27.3% of households watching with a 43% share.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Schwed |first1=Mark |url=https://variety.com/1993/tv/news/kudocast-s-nielsen-ratings-highest-in-10-years-105508/ |access-date=August 8, 2015 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |title=Kudocast's Nielsen ratings highest in 10 years |date=March 30, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119050617/http://variety.com/1993/tv/news/kudocast-s-nielsen-ratings-highest-in-10-years-105508/ |archive-date=November 19, 2015 }}</ref> At the time, it earned the lowest viewership for an Academy Award telecast and the lowest ratings for any broadcast.<ref>{{harvnb|Pond|2005|p=159}}</ref>

In July 1986, the ceremony presentation received four nominations at the [[38th Primetime Emmy Awards|38th Primetime Emmy]]s.<ref>{{cite news|title=Primetime Emmy Award database |url=http://www.emmys.com/shows/58th-annual-academy-awards |access-date=April 29, 2014 |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts and Sciences]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119105212/http://www.emmys.com/shows/58th-annual-academy-awards |archive-date=November 19, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Nominations for Prime-Time Emmys |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1986-08-01-ca-18965-story.html |access-date=June 9, 2015 |work=Los Angeles Times |url-access=subscription |date=August 1, 1986 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308022240/http://articles.latimes.com/1986-08-01/entertainment/ca-18965_1_prime-time-emmys/3 |archive-date=March 8, 2016 }}</ref> The following month, the ceremony won one of those nominations for Outstanding Art Direction for a Variety Program (Roy Christopher).<ref>{{cite news|last1=Margulies |first1=Lee |title=First Round : Fields, Olivier Shows Win Emmys |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1986-09-08-ca-13124-story.html |access-date=June 9, 2015 |date= September 8, 1986 |work=Los Angeles Times |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150921191648/http://articles.latimes.com/1986-09-08/entertainment/ca-13124_1_laurence-olivier/2 |archive-date=September 21, 2015 }}</ref>
